_comment: Import this egg into Pelican Panel (Admin → Eggs → Import) or Pterodactyl (Nests → Import Egg).
name: Telegram Support Suite
author: support-suite@localhost
description: Telegram AI/FAQ support bot + web admin panel + customer download portal. Single Node.js process, SQLite storage, everything persistent lives in data/.
startup: bash -c 'export GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0; if [ "${AUTO_UPDATE}" = "1" ] && [ -d .git ]; then echo "[auto-update] pulling latest..."; git fetch --all --prune && git reset --hard "origin/$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)" && CI=1 npm ci --omit=dev --no-audit --no-fund; fi; exec node src/index.js'

installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
# Telegram Support Suite installer — fully non-interactive, reinstall-safe.
set -e
export GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0
export CI=1
export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

apt-get update -qq >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
apt-get install -y -qq git ca-certificates >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

mkdir -p /mnt/server
cd /mnt/server

REPO_HOST_PATH="github.com/${GITHUB_USERNAME}/${GITHUB_REPO}.git"
if [ -z "${GITHUB_PAT}" ] || [ -z "${GITHUB_USERNAME}" ]; then
    echo "ERROR: GITHUB_USERNAME and GITHUB_PAT variables are required (the repository is private)."
    echo "Create a fine-grained PAT with read-only Contents access to the repo and set both variables."
    exit 1
fi
CLONE_URL="https://${GITHUB_USERNAME}:${GITHUB_PAT}@${REPO_HOST_PATH}"

if [ -d .git ]; then
    echo "[install] existing checkout found — updating (data/ is never touched)"
    git remote set-url origin "${CLONE_URL}"
    git fetch --all --prune
    git reset --hard "origin/${GITHUB_BRANCH}"
else
    echo "[install] cloning branch ${GITHUB_BRANCH}..."
    git clone --branch "${GITHUB_BRANCH}" --single-branch "${CLONE_URL}" .
fi

if ! git rev-parse HEAD >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "ERROR: clone failed — check GITHUB_USERNAME/GITHUB_PAT/GITHUB_REPO/GITHUB_BRANCH."
    exit 1
fi

echo "[install] installing dependencies..."
if ! npm ci --omit=dev --no-audit --no-fund; then
    echo "[install] npm ci failed once — retrying with a rebuild of native modules"
    npm ci --omit=dev --no-audit --no-fund || { echo "ERROR: npm install failed"; exit 1; }
fi
npm rebuild better-sqlite3 >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

mkdir -p data

echo "[install] done. Start the server, then open http://YOUR-NODE-IP:PORT/admin/login"
echo "[install] the first-boot admin password prints in the server console if ADMIN_PASSWORD was left empty."

variables.name: Telegram bot token
variables.description: From @BotFather on Telegram. Also disable Group Privacy there so the bot can read group messages.

variables.name: GitHub username
variables.description: Owner of the private repository (for cloning).

variables.name: GitHub personal access token
variables.description: Fine-grained PAT with read-only Contents access to the repository. Needed because the repo is private.

variables.name: GitHub repository
variables.description: Repository name that contains the app.

variables.name: AI endpoint base URL
variables.description: OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Ollama on the same node: http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1 (can be changed later in the panel).

variables.name: AI model
variables.description: Model name on your endpoint, e.g. llama3.1 (Ollama) or llama-3.3-70b-versatile (Groq).

variables.name: AI API key
variables.description: Only if your endpoint needs one (local Ollama does not).

variables.name: Admin username
variables.description: First admin account for the web panel (created on first boot only).

variables.name: Admin password (initial)
variables.description: Initial panel password — you must change it at first login. Leave empty to auto-generate (printed once in the server console).

variables.name: Public URL
variables.description: Address customers use to reach the portal, e.g. http://1.2.3.4:25580 or https://portal.example.com — used in links the bot sends.

variables.name: Auto-update on start
variables.description: 1 = git pull + npm ci on every start. Data is never touched.

variables.name: Max upload size (MB)
variables.description: Largest file the admin panel accepts for the download area.
